nodes.label: Proof of skill beats presentation polish
nodes.visual: One continuous tabletop moment — pen, napkin, coffee ring, no cutaways to faces.
nodes.summary: Every node in this board either supports this sentence or gets cut. The edit is 19 seconds long, so nothing decorative survives.

nodes.label: Your first client doesn't come from a perfect portfolio
nodes.visual: Bold caption on a dark frame; the word 'perfect' gets struck through the moment it is spoken.

nodes.label: A portfolio is a presentation, not a proof
nodes.visual: Caption only. No portfolio mockups — mocking one up makes the video look like the thing it is arguing against.

nodes.label: Mine came from a napkin sketch in a coffee shop
nodes.visual: Top-down close-up: pen drawing on a real napkin, coffee cup edge in frame, hand entering from the right.

nodes.label: The napkin is the hero object
nodes.visual: One real napkin appears in every scene, in the same light, and is reused for the CTA — a single object holding the whole 19 seconds together.

nodes.label: I drew the logo right in front of her
nodes.visual: Same shot, tighter: the pen completes the mark; a second pair of hands slides the napkin closer.

nodes.label: Stop waiting to look professional
nodes.visual: Caption takes the whole frame. Cut the music dead for one beat before it lands.

nodes.label: Start showing people you can solve their problem
nodes.visual: Return to the napkin, slow push-in; captions land one phrase per beat and hold 1.5s past the voiceover.

nodes.label: Stock-footage hands would kill the whole argument
nodes.visual: Any b-roll hands that look bought undercut 'real proof'. If filming fails, use a photo of the actual sketch instead.
nodes.summary: This is the one note the editor must not ignore: the moment the napkin looks stock, the message inverts.

nodes.label: One 10-minute phone session, hands only
nodes.visual: Table by a window, natural light, phone clamped overhead. No faces, no second location, no new purchases.

nodes.label: Polish takes weeks; proof takes one conversation
nodes.visual: The edit stays slow and untouched during the story, then snaps tight at 'She paid me' — the contrast is carried by pacing, not by effects.
